brief.outcome: Grow new patients at the two-dentist clinic from about 35 a month to 60 a month by June, with the practice able to see which of its channels brought them.

ambition.goal_beyond: A steady supply of the right new patients, for the treatments the practice most wants to do, that does not depend on one big push or on word of mouth alone
rungs: Fix the Google profile and the website enquiry path, and launch one compliant search campaign
Find where people who look for a dentist in town are lost (not seen, not enquiring, or enquiring but not booked) and fix the biggest cause first
Keep it true: a monthly check of new patients by source and of enquiry-to-booking rate that flags a drop before it costs a quarter
ambition.judge: The practice software new-patient report by month and by source (counts only), read against the 35 a month baseline and the same months a year earlier

brief.deliverable: A fixed and complete Google Business Profile, a faster enquiry path on the WordPress site with treatment pages, a compliant Google Ads search campaign launched with the owner's approval inside the budget, and a monthly readout of new patients against the 60 target

Tracking of calls, forms and booking requests checked, with no patient data sent to ad or analytics tools
Diagnosis that marks every hypothesis supported, refuted or unknown

research.approach: Practitioners treat local patient acquisition as a funnel with four leaks: not seen, not chosen, not enquiring, enquiring but not booked. They start from the raw material (the practice system's new-patient counts by source, the Google profile insights and the Search Console export) and fix what is free and fast first: a complete and accurate Google profile, one clear page per treatment, an easy way to ring or book, and a steady flow of genuine reviews. Paid search comes after tracking is trusted and after claims are checked, and starts small so cost per new patient is known before the budget grows. In UK dentistry every claim needs evidence on file, before-and-after images need signed consent, and review replies must never confirm that someone is a patient. The result is judged by the practice's own new-patient report, not by ad clicks.

sources.title: Google Business Profile Help: How to improve your local ranking
sources.note: Platform documentation: local results rest on relevance, distance and prominence; verify, keep details complete, respond to reviews, add photos. No way to pay for local ranking. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: Google Business Profile Help: Business Profile restrictions for policy violations
sources.note: Platform documentation: fake or incentivised reviews can lead to reviews being removed or profile restrictions; no rewards for reviews and no selective asking. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: ASA and CAP Advice Online: Dental general
sources.note: Regulator guidance: objective claims need evidence on file; before-and-after images must be genuine and representative with signed, dated proof; do not imply a medical qualification.

sources.title: General Dental Council: Guidance on advertising
sources.note: Regulator guidance: advertising must be accurate and not misleading; no implied specialist status; show registration details; say whether the practice is NHS, private or mixed. Read through a search summary; confirm the current text. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: Denplan: Navigating social media comments and complaints
sources.note: Dental sector advice: protect confidentiality, keep replies general and move the conversation to a private channel; never disclose patient information online, even indirectly. Article published 14 Oct 2025.

sources.title: Google Ads Help: Measure calls from ads
sources.note: Platform documentation: three ways to count calls (from ads, from the website, imported); website call tracking swaps the number for a Google forwarding number. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

sources.title: Google Ads policy: Health in personalized advertising
sources.note: Platform policy: health is a sensitive category, so site-visitor remarketing and customer-list audiences are not allowed; conversion tracking is not restricted. Only fragments were readable; confirm the current text. (no date shown on the page; accessed 2026-11-03)

steps.why: UK dental advertising needs evidence for claims, consent for images and honest titles before any copy is written.

steps.why: Each leak has a different fix and the cheapest are free.

steps.name: Fix the Google profile and run a safe review routine
steps.why: Prominence and relevance come from a complete profile and genuine, recent reviews; replies must protect confidentiality.

steps.why: Searchers choose a clinic that answers their treatment question and makes the next step easy.

steps.why: Starting small shows cost per new patient before the budget grows, and keeps wording and audiences within policy.

steps.name: Read monthly new patients and enquiry-to-booking against the baseline
steps.why: The practice report, not ad clicks, shows whether more patients arrived and from where.

steps.name: Remarket to site visitors
steps.why: Common in local advertising to win back people who looked.

pitfalls.text: Judging success by clicks or calls instead of new patients registered in the practice system.
Replying to a review in a way that confirms the reviewer is a patient or mentions treatment.
Asking only happy patients for reviews, or offering anything in return, which puts the whole profile at risk.
Ad or page claims without evidence on file, unsupported superlatives, or before-and-after photos without signed consent.
Using site-visitor remarketing or customer lists for a health service, which Google restricts and which would also move patient data out of the practice.
Buying clicks before the clinic has chair time and a fast reply to enquiries, so extra demand is lost.

stages.name: Pin down the goal
stages.goal: Turn the request into a measured goal, rules, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Set what we may say
stages.goal: Build a claims and consent register for the practice: approved claims with evidence, claims not allowed, image consent held, registration details and NHS or private statement.

checks.name: Every approved claim names the evidence held and who holds it
Unsupported superlatives, specialist titles not held and anything implying a cure are listed as not allowed
Before-and-after images are listed only where a signed, dated consent is confirmed; otherwise the count is zero

stages.name: Gather the raw counts
stages.goal: Pull new patients by month and source, profile insights, Search Console data and the enquiry tally into the data home, counts only.

checks.name: Monthly new patients cover at least 12 months and the latest 3 months average within 10% of the reported 35, or the gap is explained
Review count and rating match the live profile page (140 and 4.6 as reported)
No file contains a patient name, date of birth or contact detail
Any missing field (source, treatment, enquiry log) is named and what it blocks is listed

stages.name: Check enquiries are counted without patient data
stages.goal: List every way a person gets in touch (call, form, booking link, profile call and directions, email), check each is counted once, and design the events and consent needed before any ad spend.

checks.name: Each enquiry route has a named event or is marked untracked
A test call click and a test form send each fire exactly one event
No form field content, treatment name tied to a person, or patient identifier is sent to analytics or ad tools
Tags only fire after the cookie consent the site already shows, or the gap is stated
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the monthly readout

stages.name: Find where local searchers are lost
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses on the profile, search visibility, treatment pages, reviews, enquiry handling and chair capacity, and keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers used
A finding based on fewer than 30 impressions-weighted queries or fewer than 20 enquiries is marked low-confidence
Each main finding names a competing explanation
States the gap in patients: how many extra a month 60 needs, and how many each fix could plausibly add, or marks it unknown

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked options with expected effect on new patients, effort, confidence, risk, cost and how each will be measured, plus the spend limit and a starting budget.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect, effort, confidence, risk, cost and how it is measured
Paid options show a spend limit from the practice's own value per new patient, or say it is unknown and start at the lowest test level
Free fixes and measurement fixes rank before paid spend unless the diagnosis refutes them

stages.name: Owner and practice manager choose
stages.goal: Choose the options, the treatments to promote, the monthly budget up to 1,500 pounds, and confirm chair time for the target. Record reasons when the top option is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are in decisions.jsonl
Free new-patient appointment slots per month are stated next to the target of 60, or marked unknown
The chosen monthly budget is a number at or below 1,500 pounds

stages.name: Prepare the profile and review routine
stages.goal: Draft the Google profile changes (categories, services, hours, booking link, photos list, description) and a genuine review routine with reply drafts that never confirm anyone is a patient.

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included
Every sentence in the profile text matches the claims register
The review request is sent to every patient who is asked, with no reward and no filtering by how they feel
No reply names a person, a treatment or says they are a patient; complaints are moved to a private channel

stages.name: Write treatment pages, enquiry path and ads
stages.goal: Draft one page per chosen treatment with tap-to-call and a booking route, and Google search ads that match the pages. Check every claim before the practice sees it.

outputs.name: Page drafts and ad copy for review

checks.name: Every claim is in the claims register with evidence, or is removed
No before-and-after image is used without a signed, dated consent
No specialist title is used unless it is held; GDC registration details and the NHS or private statement appear on the page
Each ad group matches one page and its main promise
Phone number or booking button is visible without scrolling on a 375 pixel wide screen
The campaign plan uses no remarketing lists or customer lists

stages.optional_when: No page or ad option was chosen.

stages.name: Apply changes and launch, paused first
stages.goal: Apply approved profile changes, hand over page drafts for the practice to publish, and create the search campaign paused with the approved budget cap. Register the tracking plan and the comparison before anything goes live.

checks.name: The campaign was created paused and read back from the account
Daily budget times days in the month is at or below 1,500 pounds, and the cap is shown on the receipt
Location is the town area only, with no remarketing or customer lists
The comparison (new patients each month against the 35 baseline and the same months a year earlier) is registered in experiments.jsonl before anything goes live
Profile and page changes go live before the ads, so their effect can be told apart

stages.name: Read new patients each month
stages.goal: Each month, read new patients by source, enquiry-to-booking rate and cost per new patient against the baseline, and check every guardrail.

checks.name: New patients come from the practice report, not from ad or profile clicks
Each month is compared with the 35 baseline and the same month a year earlier
Review rating is at least 4.6, spend is at most 1,500 pounds and cost per new patient is under the practice's own value figure
A verdict is given only after at least 3 full months; before that the result is INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the comparison, record what moved new patients and what did not, propose rules with their scope and plan the next round.

checks.name: The registered comparison is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this clinic or for any local clinic

hypotheses.statement: The Google profile is incomplete or inconsistent, so it is not matched to treatment searches.
hypotheses.test: Check the profile against the checklist (primary category, services, hours, booking link, photos, description) and compare name, address and phone on the top 5 directories.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Two or more required fields are missing or any of the top 5 directories shows a different name, address or phone.
hypotheses.refute_if: All fields are complete and the details match everywhere.

hypotheses.statement: The clinic is not showing for treatment and town searches that bring new patients.
hypotheses.test: Search Console non-brand queries with the town or treatment words: share of impressions by position.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of non-brand impressions are at position 11 or lower, or key treatments have almost no impressions.
hypotheses.refute_if: Most non-brand impressions are in the top 5 and click-through is normal for those positions.

hypotheses.statement: There is no clear page for the treatments people search for, so searches land on the home page or on rivals.
hypotheses.test: List treatments offered against pages that exist; for each, check impressions and landing page in Search Console.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Three or more treatments with search demand have no dedicated page.
hypotheses.refute_if: Each treatment with demand has a page that is the one Google shows.

hypotheses.statement: The rating is strong but reviews are not recent enough to keep the clinic in the local results.
hypotheses.test: Count reviews in the last 90 days for the clinic and the top 3 rival clinics in the same area.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The clinic has fewer recent reviews than two of the three rivals.
hypotheses.refute_if: The clinic is at or above the middle of the rivals on recent reviews.

hypotheses.statement: Enquiries are lost between contact and first appointment (missed calls, slow replies, a hard booking path).
hypotheses.test: From the two-week enquiry tally: share of enquiries that book a first appointment, share unanswered within one working day, and missed or out-of-hours calls.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Fewer than half of enquiries book, or more than 1 in 4 get no reply within a working day.
hypotheses.refute_if: Most enquiries book and nearly all get a same-day reply.

hypotheses.statement: The clinic does not have the chair time for 60 new patients a month, so more demand would be wasted.
hypotheses.test: Compare free new-patient appointment slots in a normal month with 60.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Free slots are fewer than 60 a month, or the wait for a first appointment is already longer than the practice wants.
hypotheses.refute_if: At least 60 first-appointment slots are free each month with an acceptable wait.

hypotheses.statement: Most new patients arrive by recommendation or other routes, so search can add less than the target needs.
hypotheses.test: New patients by how they heard of the practice, from the practice report.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than half of new patients come from recommendation or referral and search is a small share.
hypotheses.refute_if: Search and the profile already bring a large share and are growing.

hypotheses.statement: A 1,500 pound monthly budget cannot bring 25 extra patients at an acceptable cost per patient.
hypotheses.test: After 2 months of data: spend divided by new patients from search, against the practice's own value per new patient. Before launch, a range from the Google Ads planner and the observed enquiry-to-booking rate.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cost per new patient from search is above the value per new patient, or the budget at the observed rates yields fewer than 25 extra patients.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per new patient is below the value figure and the budget can reach 25 extra patients at observed rates.

dropped.reason: Calls are recorded and routed through a third party, which could move patient information out of the practice; click-to-call events and the reception tally are used instead.
Google restricts remarketing and customer lists for health services, and it would use visitor data in ad tools; outside the owner's limits.

measurement.window: Monthly, with a verdict after at least 3 full months. Compare each month with the 35 baseline and with the same month a year earlier, because dental demand has seasons.
measurement.min_volume: At least 3 months of data, and at least 20 enquiries in a month before the enquiry-to-booking rate is called a finding.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause the ads at once if the review rating drops below 4.6, spend reaches 1,500 pounds in the month, or any ad or page claim is challenged; otherwise run the full window before a verdict.
